title: Understanding and Mitigating Gradient Pathologies in Physics-Informed Neural Networks
authors_full: Sifan Wang, Yujun Teng, Paris Perdikaris
affiliations: Sifan Wang: Graduate Group in Applied Mathematics and Computational Science, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA 19104, USA; Yujun Teng: Department of Mechanical Engineering and Applied Mechanics, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA 19104, USA; Paris Perdikaris: Department of Mechanical Engineering and Applied Mechanics, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia, PA 19104, USA
subdomain: PINN training dynamics: unbalanced back-propagated gradients, gradient-flow stiffness, adaptive loss weighting; benchmark PDEs (Helmholtz, Poisson, Klein-Gordon, lid-driven cavity)
industry_context: Academic computational-physics research (Predictive Intelligence Lab, University of Pennsylvania); funded by the US Department of Energy ASCR program (grant de-sc0019116) and DARPA Physics of Artificial Intelligence (grant HR00111890034); no named company
problem_class: theory (failure-mode analysis of PINN training) demonstrated on forward-problem manufactured-solution benchmarks
physics_enforced_exact: (i) 2D Helmholtz: Delta u(x,y) + k^2 u(x,y) = q(x,y) on Omega = (-1,1)^2 with Dirichlet u = h on dOmega; exact solution u = sin(a1*pi*x) sin(a2*pi*y) with a1 = 1, a2 = 4 (source q given in eq. 10). (ii) 1D Poisson: Delta u(x) = g(x) on (0,1), u = h at x = 0 and x = 1; exact solution u(x) = sin(Cx), g(x) = -C^2 sin(Cx). (iii) Klein-Gordon (1D space + time): u_tt + alpha*u_xx + beta*u + gamma*u^k = f(x,t) with u(x,0) = g1(x), u_t(x,0) = g2(x), u(x,t) = h(x,t) on the spatial boundary; case alpha = -1, beta = 0, gamma = 1, k = 3 (cubic nonlinearity), T = 1; fabricated solution u(x,t) = x cos(5*pi*t) + (x*t)^3. (iv) Steady 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes in non-dimensional form for the lid-driven cavity: u.grad(u) + grad(p) - (1/Re) Delta u = 0 and div(u) = 0, with u = (1,0) on the lid Gamma_1 and u = (0,0) on the other three walls Gamma_0; Re = 100.
pde_type: multiple (elliptic: Helmholtz, Poisson; hyperbolic: Klein-Gordon; incompressible Navier-Stokes: lid-driven cavity)
nonlinearity: mixed: Helmholtz and Poisson are linear; Klein-Gordon strongly nonlinear (gamma*u^3, k = 3); cavity Navier-Stokes mildly nonlinear (convective term at Re = 100)
bcs_ic_handled: All auxiliary data imposed as soft MSE penalty terms: L_ub over N_b boundary points (Dirichlet data g_b) and L_uo over N_0 initial points (initial data h_0), eqs. 5-7; cavity: u = (1,0) on the moving lid, u = (0,0) on the remaining walls; Klein-Gordon: g1 = g2 = 0 initial data plus Dirichlet values extracted from the fabricated solution; no Neumann/flux cases; in the streamfunction-pressure cavity variant, incompressibility is satisfied exactly by construction instead of being penalized.
enforcement_mechanism: soft-penalty (autodiff PDE residual MSE at collocation points plus MSE data-fit terms, with adaptive per-term weights via learning-rate annealing); one hybrid hard-constraint element: streamfunction output transform makes div(u) identically zero
enforcement_details: Residual r_theta(x,t) := d/dt f_theta(x,t) + N_Delta[f_theta](x,t) (eq. 3) evaluated by reverse-mode automatic differentiation at collocation points and minimized as L_r = (1/N_r) sum |r_theta|^2. Diagnostics: per-layer histograms of back-propagated gradients grad_theta L_r vs grad_theta L_ub, and largest Hessian eigenvalue sigma_max(grad^2_theta L); gradient descent is the forward Euler discretization of the gradient flow, stable only for eta < 2/sigma_max. Mitigation 1 (Algorithm 1): per-term effective learning-rate rescaling lambda_i updated online from gradient statistics. Mitigation 2: streamfunction representation (u,v) = (dpsi/dy, -dpsi/dx) eliminates the continuity residual but requires third-order derivatives of the network.
network_architecture: M1/M2: standard fully-connected MLP, 3-7 hidden layers with 30/50/100 units (typical study: 4-5 layers x 50 units). Proposed modified architecture (M3/M4): two extra encoder subnetworks on the inputs U = phi(X W^1 + b^1), V = phi(X W^2 + b^2); first layer H^(1) = phi(X W^{z,1} + b^{z,1}); gated residual propagation Z^(k) = phi(H^(k) W^{z,k} + b^{z,k}), H^(k+1) = (1 - Z^(k)) (elementwise-multiply) U + Z^(k) (elementwise-multiply) V for k = 1..L; output f_theta(x) = H^(L+1) W + b (eqs. 43-47); inspired by neural attention mechanisms; essentially the same parameters as a standard FCN plus the two encoders; small computational/memory overhead per forward pass.
input_representation: (x,y) spatial coordinates (Helmholtz, cavity) or space-time (x,t) (Klein-Gordon); X is the n x d design matrix; inputs feed both the main trunk and the two encoder networks of the modified architecture; no auxiliary features (no distance functions or parameter embeddings)
output_representation: u(x,y) for Helmholtz/Poisson; u(x,t) for Klein-Gordon; cavity velocity-pressure variant outputs [u(x,y), v(x,y), p(x,y)]; cavity streamfunction-pressure variant outputs [psi(x,y), p(x,y)] with (u,v) = (dpsi/dy, -dpsi/dx) computed by automatic differentiation (hard incompressibility)
loss_terms: General: L(theta) = L_r(theta) + sum_{i=1..M} lambda_i L_i(theta) (eqs. 4/35/37), with L_r = (1/N_r) sum |r_theta(x_r^i, t_r^i)|^2 (eq. 5), L_ub = (1/N_b) sum |u(x_b^i, t_b^i) - g_b^i|^2 (eq. 6), L_uo = (1/N_0) sum |u(x_0^i, 0) - h_0^i|^2 (eq. 7). Helmholtz: L = L_r + lambda_ub L_ub (eq. 11). Poisson: L = L_b + L_r with second-derivative residual (eq. 13). Klein-Gordon: L = L_r + lambda_ub L_ub + lambda_uo L_uo (eq. 54). Cavity velocity-pressure: L = L_ru + L_rv + L_rc + L_ub + L_vb (eq. 62) (two momentum residuals plus a continuity residual). Cavity streamfunction-pressure: L = L_ru + L_rv + L_ub + L_vb (eq. 70), continuity term eliminated.
loss_weighting: Model M1: fixed unit weights (original Raissi formulation). Proposed Algorithm 1 (M2/M4): instantaneous weights lambda_hat_i = max|grad_theta L_r(theta_n)| / mean(|grad_theta L_i(theta_n)|) (eq. 40), smoothed by moving average lambda_i <- (1 - alpha) lambda_i + alpha lambda_hat_i (eq. 41), recommended hyper-parameters eta = 1e-3 and alpha = 0.9, updated every 10 gradient-descent steps; accuracy insensitive for alpha in [0.5, 0.9]; learned weights are large: lambda_ub ~ 150-350 (Helmholtz, Fig. 8), lambda_uo ~ 50-100 and lambda_ub ~ 150-400 (Klein-Gordon, Fig. 16)
sampling_strategy: collocation points randomly/uniformly placed inside the domain; boundary and initial data points prescribed; stiffness experiments sample all collocation points uniformly from both boundary and interior; primer notes residual/boundary points can be re-randomized at every gradient step with large budgets (C ~ 1e4-1e8); exact per-benchmark point counts not stated; mini-batch size 128
optimizer_schedule: Adam optimizer with default settings, 40,000 stochastic-gradient iterations for every benchmark, single precision; Sec. 2.2 Helmholtz illustration: Adam with initial learning rate 1e-3 and a decreasing annealing schedule; Sec. 2.4 stiffness study: full-batch gradient descent, initial learning rate 1e-3 with exponential decay rate 0.9 and decay step 1,000 iterations; lambda weights updated every 10 iterations (Algorithm 1)
training_compute: Lenovo X1 Carbon ThinkPad laptop, Intel Core i5 2.3 GHz processor, 8 GB RAM; Klein-Gordon wall-clock time for 40,000 iterations (Table 3): M1 200 s, M2 200 s, M3 760 s, M4 1040 s
data_regime: physics-only (no observational data): PDE residual at collocation points plus exact Dirichlet/initial values from manufactured solutions; reference data only for the cavity, generated in-house by a finite-difference streamfunction-vorticity solver (N = 128 grid, second-order discretization, Wood's formula for the vorticity boundary condition, convergence criterion eps = 1e-4)
datasets_used: self-constructed manufactured-solution benchmarks: 2D Helmholtz on (-1,1)^2 (u = sin(pi x) sin(4 pi y)); 1D Poisson with u = sin(Cx), C in {1, 2, 4}; Klein-Gordon with u(x,t) = x cos(5 pi t) + (x t)^3 on [0,1] x [0,1], T = 1; 2D lid-driven cavity at Re = 100 (finite-difference reference solution)
baselines_compared: Model M1 = original Raissi et al. 2019 PINN formulation (composite soft loss, unit weights) used as the baseline in every benchmark; internal comparison across the four variants M1-M4 (original / +learning-rate annealing / +modified architecture / both); no external classical-solver accuracy comparison (the in-house finite-difference solver only generates the cavity reference field)
evaluation_metrics: relative L2 error of predicted vs exact solution (point-wise absolute error fields also shown); per-layer histograms of back-propagated gradients of each loss term; largest Hessian eigenvalue sigma_max(grad^2_theta L); wall-clock training time (s)
key_quantitative_results: - Helmholtz (4 hidden layers x 50 units, 40,000 iterations): M1 rel. L2 = 1.81e-01 (15.7%); learning-rate annealing (M2) 1.27e-02; modified architecture (M3) 5.69e-03; over 9 architectures (3/5/7 layers x 30/50/100 units, 10 seeds each) M1 errors span 8-31% while M4 is best in every configuration (Table 2: 1.49e-03 to 1.67e-02; text quotes 0.12-0.25%); best cell 100 units/7 layers: M1 8.14e-02 -> M4 1.49e-03. - Klein-Gordon (5 layers x 50 units, Table 3): M1 1.79e-01 (17.9%), M2 1.06e-02, M3 1.97e-02, M4 2.81e-03 (Fig. 15 run reports 2.22e-03, max absolute error 0.004); training time M1/M2 200 s vs M3 760 s and M4 1040 s. - Stiffness: eigenvalues of grad^2_theta L reach 1e6, dominated by L_r; sigma_max(grad^2_theta L) ~ 1e5-1e6 for anisotropic Helmholtz (a2 = 4) vs ~ 1e3-1e4 for isotropic (a2 = 1); the modified architecture lowers the leading Hessian eigenvalue by roughly 3x. - Lid-driven cavity (Re = 100): velocity-pressure representation fails for all models (rel. L2 7.48e-01 to 7.84e-01); streamfunction-pressure representation: M1 2.71e-01, M2 2.49e-01, M3 1.21e-01, M4 3.42e-02 (~3%).
errors_reported: Helmholtz: M1 1.81e-01, M2 1.27e-02, M3 5.69e-03 (4x50 network); Table 2 sweep: M1 from 2.44e-01 to 8.14e-02 vs M4 from 1.67e-02 to 1.49e-03. Klein-Gordon (Table 3): M1 1.79e-01, M2 1.06e-02, M3 1.97e-02, M4 2.81e-03. Cavity velocity-pressure (Fig. 17): M1 7.84e-01, M2 7.48e-01, M3 7.48e-01, M4 7.53e-01. Cavity streamfunction-pressure (Fig. 18): M1 2.71e-01, M2 2.49e-01, M3 1.21e-01, M4 3.42e-02.
speedup_claims: No runtime speedup claimed; headline accuracy claim: improve the predictive accuracy of physics-informed neural networks by a factor of 50-100x across a range of problems in computational physics (abstract and Sec. 3); learning-rate annealing adds negligible wall-clock cost (Klein-Gordon: 200 s vs 200 s for M1) while the modified architecture costs roughly 4-5x more (760-1040 s)
ablations: (1) Poisson stiffness parameter C in {1,2,4}: larger C gives a more pronounced gradient imbalance and inaccurate reconstruction; (2) Helmholtz anisotropy a2 = 1 vs 4: anisotropic target makes the gradient flow markedly stiffer (sigma_max 1e5-1e6 vs 1e3-1e4); (3) architecture sweep 3/5/7 hidden layers x 30/50/100 units, averaged over 10 random seeds (Table 2); (4) M1/M2/M3/M4 factor decomposition including training-time cost (Table 3); (5) sensitivity to moving-average coefficient alpha stable on [0.5, 0.9], lambda updated every 10 steps; (6) velocity-pressure vs streamfunction-pressure output representation for the cavity.
stated_limitations: - 'we have to admit that we are still at the very early stages of rigorously understanding the capabilities and limitations of physics-informed neural networks' (Sec. 4), with open questions: relation between PDE stiffness and gradient-flow stiffness, whether stiffness can be reduced (domain decomposition, loss formulations, architectures), more stable optimization algorithms, and the effect of stiffness on approximation and generalization error. - 'in absence of a universal approximation theorem for physics-informed neural networks ... it is currently unclear whether standard fully-connected architectures offer sufficiently flexible representations for inferring the solution of complex PDEs' (Sec. 2.6). - Velocity-pressure PINN: solutions inferred by minimizing the composite loss 'will not exactly satisfy prescribed boundary conditions, nor the incompressibility constraint, potentially giving rise to issues of non-uniqueness' (Sec. 3.4). - Streamfunction formulation 'incurs a larger computational cost since third-order derivatives of the neural network are needed' (Sec. 3.5). - Hand-tuned fixed lambda weights are 'extremely tedious' and not transferable across different PDEs (Sec. 2.5); 'Adam may be a poor, or even unstable choice for training physics-informed neural networks' (Sec. 2.4); implicit/IMEX splitting, proximal and competitive-gradient alternatives deferred to future work.
failure_modes: unbalanced back-propagated gradients: boundary/initial-loss gradients concentrate sharply around zero and attain much smaller magnitudes than residual-loss gradients, biasing the network toward small PDE residual with violated boundary conditions and erroneous predictions; numerical stiffness: many Hessian eigenvalues up to 1e6 force tiny stable learning rates (eta < 2/sigma_max) and can make L(theta_{n+1}) - L(theta_n) > 0 so gradient descent fails to decrease the loss even in the descent direction (oscillating L_r, Fig. 4b); high architecture sensitivity of vanilla PINNs (8-31% error spread over 9 configurations x 10 seeds); formulation-induced failure: velocity-pressure cavity representation cannot produce a reasonable approximation for any of M1-M4 (~0.75 rel. L2) because incompressibility/BC are not exactly satisfied (non-uniqueness).
reproducibility: Code and data publicly available at https://github.com/PredictiveIntelligenceLab/GradientPathologiesPINNs; implemented in TensorFlow; single precision, mini-batch 128, Adam default settings, Glorot initialization, tanh activations; recommended hyper-parameters eta = 1e-3 and alpha = 0.9 printed in Algorithm 1; Table 2 results averaged over 10 independent trials with randomized weight initializations; all runs on one laptop CPU.
quotable_finding: Our analysis reveals a fundamental mode of failure in physics-informed neural networks related to stiffness in the gradient flow dynamics. (p. 2)
relevance_rqs: RQ2: canonical evidence for loss-weighting and architecture as trainable PINN components (Algorithm 1 adaptive weights; modified FCN; M1-M4 ablation); RQ3: mechanistic account of how soft-penalty physics enforcement generates gradient imbalance and stiffness (gradient histograms, Hessian spectra, gradient bounds eqs. 14-15 and 33-34); RQ4: reliability/training-failure analysis including a negative result (velocity-pressure cavity) and an open-problems agenda; RQ1 marginally: forward math benchmarks only, no industrial application.
manuscript_section: S4 methods (adaptive loss weighting, optimizer schedules, architecture modifications); component/loss-weighting tables; the training-reliability and failure-modes subsection; motivating context for the NTK-weighting and self-adaptive PINN papers
cross_paper_links: builds-on: PINN-A01 (Raissi, Perdikaris & Karniadakis 2019, ref. [12]) - the original PINN formulation is the M1 baseline analyzed throughout; inspired-by: attention mechanisms (Vaswani et al. 2017, ref. [45]) for the gated-residual architecture; related adaptive-weighting precedent: GradNorm (Chen et al. 2018, ref. [52]) for multi-task loss balancing; same-group follow-up addressing the same imbalance via neural tangent kernels = PINN-A06 (not cited in this preprint, natural successor); no interaction with DeepONet/FNO/XPINN
notes_caveats: Analyzed PDF is the arXiv:2001.04536v1 preprint (13 Jan 2020) printed under the title 'Gradient Pathologies'; the published SIAM version (2021) is titled 'Gradient Flow Pathologies'. All four case studies are manufactured-solution math benchmarks (1D-2D, at most 2D+time with T = 1, cavity Re = 100): no experimental data and no external-solver error comparison. Text/table inconsistencies flagged: Sec. 3.1 text says M4 Helmholtz errors 0.12-0.25% while the Table 2 M4 column spans 1.49e-03 to 1.67e-02 (0.15-1.67%); Table 3 gives M4 Klein-Gordon 2.81e-03 while the Fig. 15 caption reports 2.22e-03 (different runs). The 50-100x improvement factor corresponds to the best M1->M4 configurations, not uniformly across all 9 Helmholtz configurations (some are ~15x). No UQ, no domain decomposition, no transfer learning. Dossier bookkeeping: same paper is also registered as slice-B record B03.
